mainEntity.name: What's the difference between an assault bike workout and traditional cycling?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in the full-body engagement and air-based resistance. Traditional cycling primarily targets the lower body, while an assault bike incorporates arm handles that move with your leg pedals, activating your upper body and core. The fan-based resistance provides an 'unlimited' challenge – the harder you push, the more resistance you encounter. This makes assault bike training a superior tool for metabolic conditioning and calorie expenditure compared to a stationary bike, which typically offers fixed resistance levels.
acceptedAnswer.description: Assault bike workouts engage both arms and legs with air-based resistance for a full-body challenge, unlike traditional cycling which is primarily lower body focused.
